title: Finding freelance clients through acquaintances, not freelance sites
why: Best clients come from personal network acquaintances; freelance marketplaces force price competition and endless grinding for work.

title: Eurosceptic opinion on the EU
why: Political opinion essay arguing the EU is a cult-like ideology; argument without substantive learning.

title: Lineage of realtime visual music programming tools
why: Traces Hookup, Image/ine and Isadora from MIT and STEIM, showing how early realtime visual languages shaped music performance software.

title: Childhood discovery of programming via cheat devices
why: Personal nostalgia story about learning through Action Replay codes; little technical explanation of how the codes work.

title: Why news sites need ads and messy photo sources
why: Insider view: ad revenue needs and poor user-submitted images constrain news site design more than polished mockups admit.

title: Emails defending a researcher in a Tor dispute
why: Quotes personnel emails in a contested accusation; a dispute about people, not technical learning.

title: How PostScript LaserWriter enabled WYSIWYG desktop publishing
why: Apple licensed PostScript from Adobe; WYSIWYG printing of screen content made MacPaint and MacWrite desktop publishing work.

title: Argentine currency controls and dollar arbitrage
why: Partisan political rant on Argentine inflation and exchange controls; unverified claims dominate the few mechanics described.

title: How bulk bandwidth pricing and fiber capacity scale
why: Transit prices fall sharply with commit size and competition, while capacity per fiber strand keeps growing, unlike fiber's real-estate value.

title: Personal account of Venezuela's political crisis
why: Political testimony on repression and elections; advocacy rather than technical or transferable learning.

title: Parent's warning about grooming on Roblox
why: Personal safety anecdote and advocacy to block the platform; emotionally important but not a transferable technical lesson.

title: Complaints about degraded Google search quality
why: Anecdotal frustration with query rewriting and CAPTCHAs; no explanation of the underlying causes.

title: Call for a new declaration of data rights
why: Advocacy quoting a list of privacy harms; a policy opinion without new technical or factual insight.

title: Personal results from 16/8 fasting
why: Personal health anecdote with self-reported results and no controlled data; claims cannot be checked from the comment.

title: Complaint about laggy modern Notepad
why: Rant about Windows apps being slow, with links to rendering demos; mostly outrage rather than explanation.

title: Undocumented tools slow large organizations
why: Opinion that large organizations must write things down; general complaint without a concrete method or mechanism.

title: Why AlphaGo's moves defy human Go chunking
why: Human players reason with chunked group abstractions; AlphaGo seems to evaluate stones more individually, producing moves outside classical theory.

title: Self-study path for relearning undergraduate math
why: Master fundamental ideas deeply via Feynman's number chapter, then learn problem-solving tricks; probability and Bayesian reasoning matter most.

title: Why off-grid sites should accept some downtime
why: Above a reliability threshold, battery production's fossil energy exceeds the solar energy saved, so chasing 100% uptime is counterproductive.

title: Comparing US and Canadian immigration rates
why: Politically charged argument built on per-capita comparisons and a self-corrected statistic; persuasion rather than learning.

title: How HN title moderation follows its guidelines
why: Moderator explanation of title editing policy; a community moderation note rather than technical content.

title: Critique of NYT coverage of Breonna Taylor case
why: Legal and political argument about media framing and constitutional rights; partisan analysis rather than technical learning.

title: Blind wine tastings reveal price doesn't predict preference
why: In blind tests a $5 Barefoot beat a $100 Silver Oak; expectations and labels strongly shape perceived quality.

title: Developers as the autoworkers of our generation
why: Extended devil's-advocate essay comparing software pay to historical labor; opinion driven, not substantive learning.

title: Why non-compete agreements should be banned
why: Policy argument distinguishing NDAs, IP assignment and non-competes; persuasive opinion rather than new knowledge.

title: How an SNI-host mismatch let Lantern masquerade traffic
why: Cloudflare did not verify the SNI field matched the encrypted Host header, letting clients impersonate customers; fixed by matching them.

title: Lifecycle costs of nuclear versus wind and solar
why: Opinion piece touching on storage and uranium purity; claims are asserted rather than quantified or explained.

title: Critique of the work-life balance framing
why: Philosophical essay on whether work should be optional; opinion without concrete evidence or method.

title: Argument that model weights should be illegal
why: Polemic arguing AI training violates copyright by analogy to Napster; legal advocacy without substantive analysis.

title: Family impact of HP layoffs
why: Personal story about a father's job and family healthcare risk; sympathetic but with no transferable lesson.

title: A scraper that won a house purchase
why: Entertaining personal anecdote about automating alerts; the lesson is thin and mostly storytelling.

title: Critique of Google abandoning XMPP for chat
why: Opinion on Google's chat strategy and protocol choices; a grievance rather than a deep technical explanation.

title: Opinion on declining trust in institutions
why: General sociopolitical commentary about US institutions; no specific evidence or mechanism offered.

title: Personal view on NHS underfunding and waits
why: Personal experience and political opinion on UK healthcare; advocacy rather than transferable knowledge.

title: Evolutionary speculation about teen girls' cruelty
why: Speculative evolutionary psychology theory on social behavior; provocative conjecture without evidence.

title: Rebuttal to claims that computers got slower
why: Rant responding to a prior article; argues by anecdote and dismissal rather than explaining latency causes.

title: Speculation on Mercedes liability and regulatory strategy
why: Opinion on whether liability promises are regulatory moats; strategic speculation without technical content.

title: Finding climate-tech engineering jobs via conference exhibitors
why: Browse exhibitor and speaker lists from storage, solar, wind, nuclear and EV conferences to find companies hiring engineers.

title: Why extensions shouldn't request access to all sites
why: Requesting every website is a large overreach; localhost web servers are hard to secure, so native messaging is the better design.

title: Argument against employer-provided health insurance
why: Opinion on tax breaks and job lock; reasonable economics but argumentative and not a substantive explanation.

title: Lessons from a JSON-file database in production
why: Concurrent writes, corruption and slow queries forced a chain of hacks ending in a single-table SQLite kitchen sink; a cautionary first-hand account.

title: Personal story of rural schooling and talent
why: Personal anecdote about inequality in education; sincere but without a transferable lesson.

title: Mechanic's account of stopping a bad contract
why: Anecdote about internal protest in a non-tech business; not technical and loosely related to the topic.

title: Business value versus code quality in legacy systems
why: Sardonic back-and-forth on whether messy code matters; opinion more than an actionable method.

title: Critique of DuckDuckGo's contrast and fixed headers
why: Design opinion about contrast and header size; preference-driven critique without rigorous evidence.

title: Why file uploads reject HEIC photos
why: Client-side file input checks extensions against an allowlist lacking HEIC, so iPhone photos are rejected before upload.

title: Soft-skill books versus learning computer science
why: Opinion that classic soft-skill books are overrated and that algorithms, math and paradigms are better investments.

title: Anecdote about a happy, curious colleague
why: Personal reflection on attitude and curiosity; inspiring but without concrete, transferable technique.

title: Agile practices causing developer burnout
why: Personal frustration with sprint ceremonies and churn; opinion about management rather than technical learning.

title: Why rotating video artifacts reveal gimbal lock
why: Near 90 degrees pitch, gimbal lock forces a roll flip; if only the object spins while background stays still, it is attached to the camera.

title: Crypto acceptance as marketing signal
why: Speculation that climate backlash will make crypto a reputational liability; market commentary without technical substance.

title: Astrology and psychics versus therapy
why: Opinion on whether astrology helps; a debate about belief and therapy rather than explanation of a method.

title: Cookies are Set-Cookie headers, not placed files
why: Servers send Set-Cookie headers and browsers choose whether to store and return them; the placing idiom misleads about who controls cookies.

title: Stripe cofounder clarifies billing fee changes
why: Company response defending a pricing change and product rationale; corporate communication rather than general knowledge.

title: Retool's response on fakercloud links
why: Company apology and incident explanation about template data; a reply that only makes sense in its thread.

title: Why iOS barriers protect native app quality
why: Opinion that developer fees and native controls improve app quality; persuasive commentary without new technical knowledge.

title: Proposal for mass testing to reopen the economy
why: Policy proposal from 2020 advocating mass rapid testing and certificates; opinion on pandemic policy rather than learning.

title: Pay is about supply, demand and timing
why: Opinion arguing that pay tracks supply, demand, timing and location rather than importance or effort; persuasive essay.

title: Taviso's Windows kernel disclosure fight with Microsoft
why: Microsoft refused out-of-band kernel patches; a simple disable-VDM mitigation was documented and published after four months of negotiation.

title: Defense of Stallman against online ostracism
why: Political essay defending a controversial figure against firing and public shaming; polemic rather than learning.

title: Pragmatic web stack: React, Django, Postgres and cookies
why: Skip Redux early, default to Postgres, use cookie auth on one domain behind nginx to avoid CORS and JWT complexity.

title: Amazon customer service and paid-review cards
why: Consumer complaint about a seller's paid-review scheme and support handling; useful warning but not transferable technical knowledge.

title: Programming communities are too mean to newcomers
why: Opinion on community hostility and inclusion; argues for empathy rather than explaining a technical topic.

title: Why plastic packaging can lower total environmental impact
why: Plastic wrap doubles cucumber shelf life, and food waste outweighs packaging; glass bottles' energy and transport often cost more than plastic.

title: VPNs shift identification to the provider's logs
why: A shared VPN IP forces an observer to combine fingerprints with provider logs, so the VPN's logging policy determines how easily you are identified.

title: Leaving CTO role after an MBA
why: Personal career story with advice against an MBA; useful reflection but largely anecdote about one person's fulfillment.

title: Argument that fuel-driven cars will remain dominant
why: Opinion on battery weight and charging; contested predictions and rhetoric rather than verified data.

title: Blogging takes years before readers arrive
why: Experience-based encouragement to blog long term; sensible advice but general motivation rather than concrete technique.

title: Linux users appreciating macOS after switching
why: Opinion about platform polish and keyboard reliability; subjective comparison without verifiable technical content.

title: IBM's incremental path from punch cards to electronics
why: IBM built and field-tested electronic calculators like the 603 and 605 before computers, showing business computing drove early electronics.

title: Question about how to master Big O fluently
why: A personal question about whether interview algorithm fluency is needed; no answer or method is given.

title: Question on REPL-style workflow outside Jupyter
why: Asks how to get Jupyter-like iterative debugging in Python; a question with no answer in the comment.

title: Telegram defends its MTProto design choices
why: Company reply to security critics about RSA and IGE; defensive corporate response rather than a self-contained explanation.

title: Why summing median task times underestimates projects
why: Task durations are right-skewed; summing medians gives a far too optimistic total because long tails dominate the sum.

title: Open source is not a privacy or security guarantee
why: Openness is a development model; closed hardware cannot be reproduced to verify builds, and open code still contains vulnerabilities.

title: Contextual summary of LK-99 superconductivity claims
why: Hype-era commentary with unverifiable historical claims about a Russian theory; the claimed material result was not reliable.

title: Why Amazon succeeded through fast fulfillment
why: Argument that speed, not catalog, drove Amazon's win; plausible business opinion with little rigorous evidence.

title: Argument for crewed Mars missions over rovers
why: Advocacy for human exploration and a global space program; policy speculation rather than technical explanation.

title: Electricity price can erase EV fuel savings
why: At $0.22/kWh a Model S costs about $0.073 per mile, the same as a 30 mpg gas car at $2.20/gallon.

title: Warning about always-on voice devices
why: Privacy opinion linking surveillance legislation to smart speakers; alarmist argument without technical analysis.

title: Confession about padding estimates and hours
why: Describes deliberately inflating estimates and faking presence; a self-admitted practice that teaches nothing valid.

title: Pitch for decentralized identity via web3
why: Promotional argument from a crypto worker for decentralized login; a pitch rather than explanation of how it works.

title: Do digital goods reduce consumer price inflation?
why: Speculative economics question about non-exclusionary goods; a hypothesis without data or conclusion.

title: Experience with .NET 5 configuration and async
why: Reviewer's frustrations with DI for config and async auth; opinion on framework design with few transferable specifics.

title: Critique of a CEO's failure narrative
why: Moral commentary on privilege after a startup shutdown; opinion about personal sympathy rather than technical learning.

title: Complaint about hiss and disappearing media formats
why: Frustration with audio hiss on non-Apple devices and lost lossless options; a rant with no diagnosis of the cause.

title: Why consumer device firmware goes unpatched
why: Devices ship on 6 to 12 month product cycles but live 3 to 5 years, and embedded OSes lack post-sale patch infrastructure.

title: Why hydrogen loses to batteries on round-trip efficiency
why: Electrolysis plus fuel cell is about 35 to 40 percent efficient, versus over 90 percent for batteries, and compression adds further losses.

title: Personal low-consumption lifestyle and energy savings
why: Personal lifestyle account with household energy figures; admirable but a personal choice rather than a transferable technique.

title: Analogy of government debt as money supply
why: Economic opinion comparing treasury debt to money; a contested argument presented as a Wile E. Coyote metaphor.

title: Why point clouds avoid needing object recognition
why: A lidar point cloud shows where something is without identifying it, so a planner can route around obstacles; cameras must recognize them.

title: Heel-striking with locked knees loads the lower back
why: Straight-legged heel landings transmit force up the leg; forefoot landings with a bent knee dissipate it, a habit minimal shoes teach.

title: Argument for gun ownership and self-defense
why: Political argument about firearms and murder rates; contested opinion rather than learning.

title: Cash-price pharmacies may cost more than insurance
why: Some $4 generics bill to insurance and count toward deductibles; cash-only pharmacies with shipping fees can cost more despite advertised savings.

title: Searle's critique of computers doing only syntax
why: Philosophical argument against AI and materialism framed by a thermostat analogy; contested position rather than explanation.

title: Personal shift to vaxxed-and-done politics
why: Political opinion about vaccine mandates and CDC statements; contested and partisan, not technical learning.

title: Proposal to disarm most police officers
why: Policy argument for unarmed compliance officers; advocacy on police reform rather than technical or factual learning.

title: Argument that affordable housing should be market-built
why: Economic and policy opinion on housing supply; persuasive argument rather than verifiable new mechanism.

title: How AppJet pivoted to Etherpad and sold to Google
why: AppJet's developer platform had almost no users; the team pivoted to Etherpad, which earned revenue before the Google Wave sale.

title: Defense of apps including third-party analytics SDKs
why: Opinion that everyone bundles analytics SDKs and the real fix is platform transparency; argumentative rather than explanatory.
